header.description: I’m a Full Stack Software Developer with commercial experience in React, TypeScript, NestJS, Node.js and MySQL. My path into software development has been gradual and consistent. Before moving fully into engineering, I spent several years in academic research and six years in professional sports analytics. This background shaped the way I work today: I’m highly analytical, data-driven and comfortable translating complex requirements into practical solutions. I’m based in Berlin, with professional English and advanced German currently progressing towards C1.

about.title: About
about.p1: I'm a Full Stack Developer based in Berlin, working mainly with React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS and MySQL.
about.p2: My path into software development has been gradual, but not accidental. I was interested in computing and programming early on, later studied Computer Science alongside my professional career, and started using Python to automate repetitive analytical tasks before moving fully into software development. Today I work as a full stack developer.
about.p3: What makes my background different is what came before software engineering.
about.p4: I hold a PhD in Physical Culture Sciences and spent several years in academic research, working with experimental and biomechanical data, analytical methods and independent research projects. Later, I spent six years in professional volleyball analytics, including Germany's Bundesliga, the CEV Champions League and Poland's top division.
about.p5: That experience still shapes how I approach software today. I enjoy understanding complex problems, structuring data, translating requirements into practical solutions and improving processes through technology.
about.p7: React | TypeScript | JavaScript | Node.js | NestJS | MySQL | PostgreSQL | MongoDB | REST APIs | SQL | Data Modelling | Docker | GitHub Actions | CI/CD | AWS | Jest | React Testing Library | Python
about.p8: I'm currently looking for Full Stack Developer / Full Stack Engineer opportunities in Germany, ideally in Berlin. I'm also open to remote roles with companies in Poland and across Europe.
about.p10: Polish native | English professional proficiency | German advanced, currently completing C1-level training.

sensorfarm.title: Full Stack Software Developer
sensorfarm.desc:
I started by diving into a map-based operations platform, working across the full stack but mostly focusing on frontend. I designed and built a dashboard that let teams visualise their operations in real time—my first real experience working within a microservices architecture.

 That experience set me up for what I'm working on now: modernising a legacy transaction platform. I'm rebuilding it from Java/JSP into React and NestJS, working directly with the CEO to shape where the product goes. What began as a single-client tool has grown into something more ambitious—a configurable platform handling complex transaction structures across multiple clients. I've designed the data architecture, built interactive analytics, and established testing practices along the way. It's been a solid progression from contributing to an established system to owning the evolution of one.

codac.title: Full Stack Web Developer
codac.desc: Full-Time on site coding bootcamp covering 840h of practical project based work in SCRUM methodology.

brv.title: Performance Data Analyst & Volleyball Statistician
brv.desc:
I worked with a coaching staff as a sports analyst, collecting and analysing match data to help them prepare and make tactical decisions. The work moved fast—typically 3-6 day competition cycles—which meant I had to quickly turn raw data into insights they could actually use on game day.

 What started as manual data processing became an opportunity to automate. I built Python scripts to clean repetitive tasks, cutting what used to take an hour down to about 10 minutes each week. It was a good lesson in identifying inefficiencies and solving them with code. The role taught me how to translate analysis into something actionable for people who needed to make real decisions under time pressure, and how to iterate based on feedback from people actually using your work.

dg.title: Performance Data Analyst & Volleyball Statistician
dg.desc: I collected and analysed match data using Data Volley to help the coaching staff prepare for each game. Every opponent required a different approach, so I adapted my analysis and reporting based on what each coach needed to see. I also automated the recurring reporting tasks using Excel and VBA, cutting 15 minutes of manual work down to under 5. That freed up time for deeper analysis work, and it meant the team could focus on strategy instead of data prep.

awf.title: Researcher & Senior Technician
awf.desc: I did my doctoral research in Sport Science, starting with a mix of teaching and research before moving into a technical role focused on experimental work and data analysis. I managed research projects end-to-end—defining research questions, recruiting study groups, collecting and preprocessing data, running analysis, and presenting findings. Most of my work centred on human balance and postural control, comparing competitive athletes against other groups. I worked with experimental and biomechanical data using Excel and MATLAB, and helped train junior colleagues on laboratory procedures and equipment.

projects.title: PROJECTS
projects.Codask: Collaborative project that aims to serve as an educational platform for students, graduates and mentors at Code Academy Berlin. It is designed to provide an opportunity for students to post questions related to coding challenges they face while learning at Code-Academy. Users can browse previously posted questions, offer solutions to other students through comments, and post new questions.
projects.ForkIt: Culinary app for people looking for new recipes and dishes to try. It relies on Spoonacular API to browse recipes from different cuisines and dish types. Users can browse recipes by categories, create own account and save favourite recipes.

footer: And finally the project you are currently looking at. It was built with NextJS. Styled with TailwindCSS, and deployed on Vercel. Hope you like it!
